title: plugin-auth: warn about SSO providers whose stored domain list holds an entry that names no domain
body:
domain:server#5 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4d1NJYFGVi2FRztyBNo

Loose ends of #33267 (#32960, #32975), review#3 nit N2 (record 6879639370).

## What is wrong

Since #33267, `POST /sso/register` and `POST /sso/update-provider` refuse a `domain` entry that is not a bare host name (a URL, a port, a path). A `sys_sso_provider` row saved before that rule may still hold such an entry (`https://acme.com`). It is not rewritten, and every rule that reads the list through the one parse (`ssoDomainEntryHosts` in `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-account-at-proven-domain.ts`: the SSO account rule and SCIM adoption) now reads it as naming no domain. Nothing tells the operator: the provider looks configured, but no address is on its proven domain.

## What to do

Make the narrowing visible for stored rows: for example a one-time boot warning (or a Setup notice) naming each provider whose `domain` list holds an entry `ssoDomainEntryNotBare` would refuse, with the fix stated in `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx` (send the bare host names as `domain` to `POST /api/v1/auth/sso/update-provider`, then verify the domain again). Reads only; no row is rewritten.

## Acceptance

- A provider stored with `https://acme.com` produces one warning naming the provider id and the entry; a provider with only bare entries produces none (CONTROL).
- No stored row changes.
